## Dataset and source

The site reads a CSV file named `cars_msrp_kaggle.csv`, hosted in a
[GitHub Gist by dvinubius](https://gist.github.com/dvinubius/33486dad2dc86319f0a06ffdb1d4f34f).
The [raw CSV](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/dvinubius/33486dad2dc86319f0a06ffdb1d4f34f/raw/)
currently contains **`r format(nrow(cars), big.mark = ",")` rows** and
**`r ncol(cars)` columns**. The project uses this hosted file; its original
collection date and methodology are not documented here, so the prices should
not be treated as current listings.

## Variables used in the site

| Dataset field | How it is used |
|---|---|
| `Make` | Vehicle manufacturer. |
| `Model` | Vehicle identification and comparison. |
| `Year` | Model year. |
| `MSRP` | Listed price, used to compare affordability. |
| `Engine HP` | Engine horsepower, used as the performance measure. |
| `highway MPG` | Highway fuel economy for the MPG charts and balance score. |
| `Vehicle Size` | Color grouping in the scatterplots. |
| `Vehicle Style` | Vehicle type used in the MPG group comparison. |

The source also includes fields such as city MPG, engine fuel type, transmission,
drive type, and popularity. The current charts focus on the fields listed above.

## Analysis notes

The site uses the available fields to compare listed price, engine horsepower,
highway fuel economy, vehicle size, and vehicle style. The balance score is a
project-specific comparison that gives equal weight to price, horsepower, and
highway fuel economy; it is not an official vehicle rating.
